candidateMCQ.questionText: In the fragment "JFIF hExif +&.%#%.&D5//5DNB>BN_UU_wqw", if the '+' character is replaced with '-', how is the visual pattern and potential parsing of the formula most likely to change?
options: The minus sign will appear, and a parser may interpret it as a subtraction operator, affecting how subsequent characters are parsed as a negative operand.
Visually nothing changes because '+' and '-' look the same in this encoded context, so parsing is unaffected.
The '-' will be treated as whitespace, so the parser will ignore it and the original parsing remains unchanged.
The replacement makes the entire string syntactically invalid, causing the parser to reject the formula.
candidateMCQ.correctAnswer: The minus sign will appear, and a parser may interpret it as a subtraction operator, affecting how subsequent characters are parsed as a negative operand.
candidateMCQ.explanation: Replacing '+' with '-' changes the symbol from a plus to a minus. Visually the character is different, and many parsers treat '-' as a subtraction or negation operator, which can alter tokenization and the meaning of the following characters. The other options either ignore the semantic role of '-' or incorrectly claim no visual change.

candidateMCQ.questionText: In the provided code fragment, the character '+' appears several times (e.g., in the segment "+&.%#%.&D5"). If every '+' were replaced with '-', which of the following best describes the expected change in the visual pattern and its potential effect on parsing?
options: The visual pattern would show hyphens instead of plus signs, and parsing might treat '-' as a subtraction operator, altering token boundaries.
The visual pattern would remain unchanged because '+' and '-' look identical in this context.
The string would become syntactically invalid, causing the entire formula to be rejected.
Only the visual appearance changes; parsing would ignore the difference between '+' and '-'.
candidateMCQ.correctAnswer: The visual pattern would show hyphens instead of plus signs, and parsing might treat '-' as a subtraction operator, altering token boundaries.
candidateMCQ.explanation: Replacing '+' with '-' changes the displayed characters from plus to hyphen. Therefore both the visual pattern and parsing behavior are affected.
